projects.title: hiro
projects.summary: The Hiro Platform offers developers building on the Stacks Protocol a unified experience for API key management, custom webhooks for real-time indexing, and deep analytics for smart-contract based applications.
projects.overview:
Early developers building on the Stacks Protocol were forced to assemble their own infrastructure before writing a line of product code: running nodes, polling for chain state, and stitching together services just to get an application off the ground.

The Hiro Platform consolidates that infrastructure into a single unified experience. Developers can provision and manage access to the Stacks API, configure webhooks to react to on-chain events, and monitor the health and usage of the services their applications depend on.

I lead product and design for the platform, partnering closely with Hiro’s Engineering and DevOps teams to shape the end-to-end developer workflow: how projects are created, how credentials are issued and scoped, how webhooks are authored and debugged, and how observability is made legible once an application is live in production.

projects.title: near.dev
projects.summary: The NEAR Developer Network was designed to provide a resource-rich and community-oriented experience to engage and support a growing developer ecosystem.
projects.overview:
Exploring, onboarding, and building on a new technology platform comes with a whole host of challenges for new and experienced developers. Regardless of the framework or platform, those considering the use of a new technology often share a set of distinct needs:

  1. Ways to effectively evaluate existing applications in order to judge the platform's potential.
  2. Practical avenues for hands-on learning getting familiar with the essential developer experience.
  3. High-quality tools and resources aimed at education, inspiring new ideas, and accelerating development.
  4. Reliable and responsive support for when they encounter challenges throughout their development journey.

These motivations led the team at Pagoda to build a new resource-rich and community-oriented experience to engage and support the developers of the NEAR Protocol ecosystem. I partnered with executive leadership to lead design strategy and end-to-end design, piloting a small team of designers, engineers and developer advocates.

projectImages.alt: A NEAR Developer Network editor-based tutorial experience.

projects.title: kit
projects.summary: Building on the success of NEAR Protocol's first web-based crypto wallet, Kit aimed to offer a more secure and refined experience for users of the platform.
projects.overview:
Before the official launch of the NEAR Protocol in 2020, NEAR's core protocol team spent the year prior building NEAR Wallet: a web-based crypto wallet utility meant to serve the protocol's first wave of new users and investors.

With a focus on simplicity and accessibility, NEAR Wallet was designed to be accessible via web browsers, and facilitated the creation of millions of NEAR accounts during its lifespan, as well as activities critical to the network such as token staking and delegation.

When the time came for the NEAR Wallet team to spin out and operate independently, I led the end-to-end design of Kit: a rebranded evolution of NEAR’s first crypto wallet that offered a more refined user experience and a greater degree of security via its implementation as a native browser extension.

featuredImage.alt: A screenshot of the Kit crypto wallet extension.

projects.title: fora
projects.summary: As the Bounties Network matured beyond a set of experiments testing new use cases for crypto incentives, it evolved into fora: a platform for community-driven initiatives and decentralized collaboration.
projects.overview:
The Bounties Network (a project by ConsenSys) was one of the first projects built on the Ethereum platform to formally experiment with crypto incentives for driving community engagement. It provided new ways for community members to earn for their contributions and supported project owners looking to source talent from an emerging decentralized workforce.

After a series of successful experiments in partnership with teams like UNICEF Innovation, the team at Bounties Network grew the platform from a white-label testing environment into a more robust community hub dubbed "fora", where people from all over the web could share about their initiatives, collaborate, and earn for their participation.

As Design Co-Founder, I owned everything from User Research and UX / Interface design to branding & identity, and even a good chunk of the front-end – taking the project from an experiment to a fully fledged product and winning a "Best Overall User Experience" award from panelists at Ethereum Devcon.
